1. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; the processor accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and the processor making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein the method includes __a technological solution implemented by the processor that goes beyond the abstract idea of merely authorizing a payment by using biometric authentication data from prior payment transactions to verify the recipient's continued existence and eligibility for the benefit payment__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing step, and wherein __the processor automatically retrieves and analyzes the biometric authentication records from the data store without human intervention__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days, and wherein __the processor compares timestamps associated with the biometric authentication to determine eligibility__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours, and wherein __the processor performs real-time verification of the biometric authentication timestamp__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein __the processor interfaces with a government benefits system to validate and process the payment__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction, and wherein __the processor retrieves biometric authentication records from financial institution databases__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction, and wherein __the processor accesses biometric authentication logs maintained by the mobile device or associated payment processor__.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made via an electronic monetary transfer to an account owned by the recipient, and wherein __the processor executes the electronic transfer through a financial network after proof-of-life verification__.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made by sending a check to the recipient, and wherein __the processor initiates a check generation and mailing process through a payment fulfillment system__.

10. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing, at a first point in time, a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor determining that the data store contains an indication that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication most recently with respect to one of said payment transactions at a second point in time earlier than the first point in time; the processor comparing a time interval defined by the second and first points in time with a pre-determined permissive time interval; the processor making the benefit payment, without requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time does not exceed the pre-determined permissive time interval; and the processor requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, prior to making the benefit payment, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time exceeds the pre-determined permissive time interval, wherein __the method includes a technological solution implemented by the processor that automatically evaluates biometric authentication recency data to determine whether additional proof-of-life verification is required, thereby reducing fraud risk and processing delays in benefit payment systems__.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is seven days, and wherein __the processor automatically calculates the time interval and compares it to the seven-day threshold without human intervention__.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is 24 hours, and wherein __the processor performs real-time interval comparison and makes automated decisions regarding proof-of-life requirements__.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein __the processor interfaces with government benefits administration systems to validate eligibility based on biometric authentication recency__.

14. (Currently amended) An apparatus comprising: a processor; and a memory in communication with the processor, the memory storing program instructions, the processor operative with the program instructions to perform functions as follows: determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein __the apparatus implements a technological solution that uses biometric authentication data from prior payment transactions to verify recipient eligibility and reduce fraud in benefit payment processing__.

15. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing, and wherein __the processor automatically filters and retrieves biometric authentication records from the pre-determined period__.

16. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days, and wherein __the processor compares transaction timestamps to the seven-day threshold__.

17. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours, and wherein __the processor performs real-time timestamp verification__.

18. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein __the processor communicates with government benefits systems__.

19. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction, and wherein __the processor retrieves biometric authentication records from financial institution data stores__.

20. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 19, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction, and wherein __the processor accesses biometric authentication logs from the mobile device or associated payment processing systems__.
